title: Add staged prompt-authoring watch-mode quickstart with structured-output linter
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Introduce a compact developer quickstart that demonstrates staged prompt authoring with an iterative watch-mode workflow and an integrated structured-output linter. Motivation: teams authoring RAG/agent prompts need a low-friction local loop to iterate on prompt stages (context assembly, skeleton generation, tool-call gating, final formatting) while validating structured outputs against a small contract. This quickstart provides: 1) a minimal file layout with a staged prompt pipeline, 2) a watch-mode devserver that hot-reloads prompt stage files and runs fast contract checks, 3) TypeScript and Go example adapters that show tool-calling guard rails, 4) an opinionated structured-output linter (StrucLint) with example contracts and fixes, 5) devcontainer + docker-compose for reproducible local runs, and 6) lightweight telemetry presets for the Console (span tags and step timing) so teams can instrument authoring iterations. The PR includes docs and a short site integration guide so the quickstart appears under "Local authoring" in the docs site nav.

Checklist completed: - scaffolding and README - TS and Go samples - watch-mode implementation and tests - StrucLint rules and example contracts - devcontainer/devops runbook - docs landing and metadata for docs site - e2e smoke CI job (headless run)

How to try locally (summary): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/staged-prompt-authoring 2) ./dev up (starts watch-mode + local indexer stub) 3) edit stages/*.prompt.json -> watch-mode runs lint and emits structured diffs 4) open http://localhost:4000/playground for a minimal REPL that shows intermediate stage outputs and tool-call proposals. See README for full commands and examples. This quickstart is intentionally minimal: it wires Redwood SDK calls via examples/samples.ts and examples/main.go but uses a stubbed indexer and a local in-memory tool adapter for safe local experimentation.
